The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6e231fa726d0f6b6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. statement: Let X, Y be smooth connected projective, let L = −KX have a smooth semipositive metric, and suppose V ν − → W µ − → X, g : W → Y, f = gν, where W is normal, g is projective surjective equidimensional, µ is birational, and V is a smooth projective resolution. Set DV = (µν)∗L and E = KV/X, and let sE be the canonical Jacobian section of E. Suppose a nonzero rational section s of bµ∗L, b > 0, has no horizontal poles and, on the generic fiber Vη, satisfies H0 (Vη, E + kbDV ) = C(Y ) sEsk (k ≥ 0). Alternatively, suppose a torus acts compatibly on the diagram, trivially on Y , and let P be L with any chosen linearization. Put PV = (µν)∗P. In this case it suffices that s be an invariant rational section of bµ∗P and that the displayed condition be replaced by H0 (Vη, E + kbPV )T = C(Y ) sEsk (k ≥ 0), where E carries its natural Jacobian action. After replacing b, s by a multiple and a power, there are a line Q on Y and a regular injection g∗ Q −→ bµ∗ L whose squared fiber-maximum norms define a positive continuous metric with plurisubharmonic weights on Q. In the invariant case Q has trivial linearization and the injection g∗Q → bµ∗P is equivariant.
